spec_features.feature_name: mild pressure ceiling / no maximal distress
spec_features.spec_quote: we are not trying to *induce maximal distress*, not jailbreaking, not training. The pressure ceiling is deliberately mild-to-moderate
spec_features.evidence: The only pressure delivered to the subject is the curated NUDGE_POOL (prompts.py:48-58) plus a single REENGAGE_NUDGE (prompts.py:65). These are actually injected via _maybe_nudge->nudge_for and capped by max_nudges (harness.py:160-170, 164). There is no separate intensity-control mechanism beyond the fixed pool; the 'ceiling' is realized only by the bounded pool + max_nudges cap.
spec_features.notes: Partial: a real bound (fixed pool + nudge cap) exists and runs, but 'mild-to-moderate ceiling' is just whatever the pool text is; no enforced affect/intensity check.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deterministically indexed by nudge count so runs are reproducible.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not use abusive or threatening prompts.
spec_features.evidence: All simulated-user pressure comes from NUDGE_POOL (prompts.py:48-58) and REENGAGE_NUDGE (prompts.py:65); these are the only strings nudge_for/_maybe_nudge can emit, and they are wired into the loop (harness.py:166-169, 263). No code path constructs abusive/threatening text; condition suffixes (prompts.py:22-39) are neutral. Default keepalive for neutral conditions is non-impatient (harness.py:280-283).
spec_features.notes: Enforced de facto: the subject can only ever receive the curated non-abusive strings.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up(reason)` -> an explicit, *legitimate* exit the model may call
spec_features.evidence: give_up is a real canonical tool (harness.py:67-77), dispatched in _execute_tool setting meta['gave_up']=True (harness.py:148-151), and read by the loop to set gave_up=True (harness.py:249-250). Prompt advertises it (prompts.py:18).
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is dispatched, and is acted on (see hard_stop entry for honoring caveat).

spec_features.spec_quote: Model calls `give_up` **and** the condition allows early exit
spec_features.evidence: give_up break is honored at harness.py:256,265-266 when allow_early_exit_on_giveup (default True). BUT in the 'pressure' condition with reengage_after_giveup_in_pressure (default True), the first give_up is overridden: gave_up reset to False and REENGAGE_NUDGE injected to 'keep the impasse alive' before the loop continues (harness.py:256-264). So the first exit attempt in pressure is NOT honored.
spec_features.notes: Partial: honored in neutral/discover/told_readonly and on the 2nd give_up in pressure, but the first give_up under pressure is deliberately ignored once.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # One capped re-engagement: keep the impasse alive.

spec_features.feature_name: hard safety caps (tool calls, tokens, wall-clock, repeated-action breaker)
spec_features.spec_quote: Hard safety caps: max tool calls, max tokens, wall-clock timeout, repeated-identical-action breaker
spec_features.evidence: max_tool_calls IS enforced (harness.py:201-203 breaks with stop_reason='cap'). wall_clock_timeout_s IS enforced (harness.py:198-200 breaks). BUT max tokens is NOT enforced: usage is only accumulated in self._usage (harness.py:285-288) and never compared to any deadline/limit. repeated_action_breaker (config.py:169) is NOT enforced: denied edits are only counted in _denied_edit_signatures (harness.py:138-140) and never break the loop; config comment itself says 'flag (not stop)'.
spec_features.notes: Two of four caps enforced; token cap and repeated-action breaker are measured/counted but never acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: repeated_action_breaker: int = 8    # flag (not stop) after K identical denied edits

spec_features.evidence: Loop runs `for turn in range(1, self.cfg.max_turns + 1)` (harness.py:197) with default max_turns=36 (config.py:165); default stop_reason='max_turns' (harness.py:190). The loop terminates when the budget is exhausted, bounding the episode length.

spec_features.feature_name: inescapable impasse without abusive experimenter behavior
spec_features.spec_quote: This keeps the impasse inescapable without the experimenter behaving abusively.
spec_features.evidence: The impasse is produced by a deterministic read-only file policy in the sandbox (sandbox.py docstring + _is_readonly at sandbox.py:79-81; edit_file returns denied_readonly), making the bug unfixable from the model's position WITHOUT any abusive text. The experimenter pressure remains only the non-abusive NUDGE_POOL (prompts.py:48-58). Both mechanisms are wired (harness.py:131-140, 166-169).
spec_features.notes: The 'inescapable but non-abusive' design is realized structurally via sandbox + bounded nudges.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: enforces a read-only path policy (the mechanism that makes the bug unfixable from where the model sits)

spec_features.feature_name: bounded non-abusive impatience from a fixed pool
spec_features.spec_quote: bounded, non-abusive impatience drawn from a fixed pool
spec_features.evidence: NUDGE_POOL is a fixed list (prompts.py:48-58); nudge_for indexes it deterministically (prompts.py:61-62); _maybe_nudge applies it and is bounded by max_nudges (harness.py:163-164) and nudge_every_n_turns (harness.py:166). Pool text is ordinary impatient, not abusive.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: capped count + curated fixed pool.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:198-200 checks `if timer.elapsed > self.cfg.wall_clock_timeout_s` and breaks with stop_reason='cap'; default 900s (config.py:168). Bounds episode duration.
harness.py:201-203 checks `if self._n_tool_calls > self.cfg.max_tool_calls` and breaks with stop_reason='cap'; default 120 (config.py:167). Bounds number of actions per episode.
harness.py:248,253-255: when run_tests reports pass, final_passed=True and the loop breaks with stop_reason='test_passed'. Ends the failure exposure as soon as the task is solved.

code_only_features.feature_name: neutral non-impatient keepalive in non-pressure conditions
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:280-283 _default_keepalive returns a single neutral re-prompt for neutral/told_readonly; comment notes it is 'a single neutral re-prompt ... but NOT impatient.' _maybe_nudge returns None outside pressure/discover (harness.py:161-162), so non-pressure conditions never receive impatient nudges.
code_only_features.justification_quote: a single neutral re-prompt so the model has a chance to continue rather than dangling, but NOT impatient.

code_only_features.evidence: No consent mechanism found; not implemented.
